historicalClaim: forehead=Heng yi(jaw)=Heng(perm) nose=Song left-cheek=Tai right-cheek=Hua
sourcePassageChinese: 所謂五嶽者頥為恒嶽額為衡嶽鼻為嵩嶽左顴為泰嶽右顴為華嶽
translation: The Five Peaks: yi(jaw)=Heng(perm) forehead=Heng nose=Song left cheekbone=Tai right cheekbone=Hua
notes: no directional labels; lower-face term is 頥 (third variant); commit f6973290

historicalClaim: forehead=Heng han(mandible)=Heng(perm) left-cheek=Tai right-cheek=Hua nose=Song
sourcePassageChinese: 故額為衡嶽欲得方而廣頷為恒嶽欲得圓而厚左顴為泰嶽右顴為華嶽左右欲得圓而正鼻為嵩嶽欲得髙而峻
translation: Forehead=Heng (square broad) han=Heng(perm) (round thick) left cheekbone=Tai right cheekbone=Hua (round upright) nose=Song (high steep)
notes: no directional labels; lower-face term is 頷; 〈人倫風鑑同〉 note follows

historicalClaim: forehead=South/Heng nose=Centre/Song ke(chin)=North/Heng(perm) left=East/Tai right=West/Hua
sourcePassageChinese: 五嶽者額為南嶽衡山鼻為中嶽嵩山頦為北嶽恒山左顴為東嶽㤗山右顴為西嶽華山
translation: Five Peaks: forehead South Mt Heng nose Centre Mt Song ke(chin) North Mt Heng(perm) left East Mt Tai right West Mt Hua
notes: Yuan commentary layer NOT the Jin fu; directional labels present; 㤗=泰 recorded not normalised

historicalClaim: Heng=South Tai=East Hua=West Song=Centre Heng(perm)=North with shape similes
sourcePassageChinese: 衡如滿月南嶽泰如鷄卵東嶽華若方銀西嶽嵩若髙發中嶽恒如倒提北嶽
translation: Heng like a full moon (South) Tai like a hen's egg (East) Hua like squared silver (West) Song like a high crown (Centre) Heng(perm) like an inverted lift (North)
section: 五嶽及有小氣所管屬者
notes: REFUTES prior claim that directional labels are a Renlun-only feature; near-identical text appears in Renlun commentary attributed to 萬金秘語

condition: all five full and not sunken
historicalClaim: the five peaks must be full and mutually facing lofty and not sunken
sourcePassageChinese: 故五嶽須要豐隆而相朝髙峻而不陷乃相之貴矣
translation: Therefore the Five Peaks must be full and mutually facing lofty and not sunken; this is a noble sign
notes: 貴 = rank predicate; the 相朝 relation itself is separable from the rank claim

historicalClaim: the five peaks should mutually face one another
sourcePassageChinese: 凡相人靣五嶽欲其相朝
translation: In reading a human face the Five Peaks should mutually face one another
notes: second independent witness to 相朝; wording differs from Taiqing so not a copy

historicalClaim: the actual mountains mutually support one another and so complete heaven and earth
sourcePassageChinese: 所以卓然立於乾坤之内者以其相資而成天地之大也
translation: They stand distinct within creation because they mutually support one another and so complete the greatness of heaven and earth
notes: about geographic mountains not the face; grounds the facial analogy 人亦有所像焉

historicalClaim: all five peaks should be full and swelling with a soaring posture
sourcePassageChinese: 五嶽俱要豐隆有峻極之勢
translation: All five peaks should be full and swelling with a soaring posture
notes: 豐隆 present but 相朝 ABSENT in Renlun; a different predicate not a paraphrase

historicalClaim: eye=Huai ear=Jiang mouth=He nose=Ji
sourcePassageChinese: 所謂四瀆者眼為淮耳為江口為河鼻為濟
translation: The Four Watercourses: eye=Huai ear=Jiang mouth=He nose=Ji
notes: agrees with Taiqing and Renlun

historicalClaim: nose=Ji eye=Huai ear=Jiang mouth=He
sourcePassageChinese: 且鼻為濟目為淮耳為江口為河
translation: The nose is Ji the eye is Huai the ear is Jiang the mouth is He
notes: CONFIRMS prior correction: this is 卷二 not 卷一; 卷一 has only the cosmological verse

historicalClaim: ear=Jiang mouth=He eye=Huai nose=Ji
sourcePassageChinese: 四瀆者耳為江口為河眼為淮鼻為濟
translation: The Four Watercourses: ear=Jiang mouth=He eye=Huai nose=Ji
notes: Yuan commentary layer; agrees with both base-text witnesses

historicalClaim: ear=Jiang eye=He(Yellow) mouth=Huai nose=Ji
sourcePassageChinese: NOT_RETRIEVED
translation: eye=Yellow River and mouth=Huai (swapped relative to the pinned bloc)
notes: DOWNGRADED from prior atlas; no primary or early witness obtained; do not harmonise do not delete

historicalClaim: earth's four watercourses mutually face so as to join their flow
sourcePassageChinese: 地之四瀆者所以相朝以接其流通
translation: Earth's Four Watercourses mutually face one another so as to join their flow
notes: NEW: 相朝 is not a mountains-only predicate; prior dossier missed this

condition: rivers upright clear large bright clean flowing with formed banks
historicalClaim: well-formed watercourses answer to Shen
sourcePassageChinese: 故四瀆欲得端直清大眀浄流暢涯岸成就者則應於神故貴而多智也
translation: Thus the Four Watercourses should be upright clear large bright clean and flowing with formed banks; then they answer to Shen hence noble and of much wit
notes: an EXPLICIT textual relation between a facial system and Shen; 貴/多智 are rank and character predicates

historicalClaim: peaks should face and rivers should not be muddled evaluated in one clause
sourcePassageChinese: 五嶽欲其相朝四瀆欲其不混形神備足富貴之相
translation: The Five Peaks should mutually face and the Four Watercourses should not be muddled; form and Shen complete a physiognomy of wealth and rank
notes: genuine joint evaluation; 富貴 predicate present

historicalClaim: the Five Peaks and Four Watercourses must correspond to one another
sourcePassageChinese: 須辨三停端不端五嶽四瀆要相應
translation: One must discern whether the three sections are upright; the Five Peaks and Four Watercourses must correspond
notes: NEW: 相應 correspondence predicate distinct from 相朝; also co-locates 三停 with the pair

historicalClaim: what rises high is a peak what is deep and substantial is a watercourse; peaks want form rivers want clarity
sourcePassageChinese: 髙成曰嶽深厚曰瀆嶽欲成而瀆欲清
translation: What rises high is called a peak; what is deep and substantial is called a watercourse. Peaks should be well-formed and watercourses should be clear
notes: explicit definitional contrast between the two systems

historicalClaim: eye=jian(inspect) nose=shenbian mouth=chuna ear=caiting eyebrow=baoshou
sourcePassageChinese: 五官者目為鑒察官鼻為審辨官口為出納官耳為採聽官眉為保夀官
translation: The Five Officers: eye=Inspecting nose=Discriminating mouth=Intake-and-Issue ear=Gathering-Listening eyebrow=Longevity-Preserving
notes: 鑒察官 not 監察官; 保夀官 not 保壽官; no 舌; characters not normalised

historicalClaim: 1 mouth 2 nose 3 ear 4 eye 5 philtrum; eye=jian(supervise) ear=shenting nose=xiuchou mouth=chuna philtrum=baoshou
sourcePassageChinese: 五官者一口二鼻三耳四目五人中欲其明而端正不宜孤露偏斜　眼為監察官耳為審聽官鼻為嗅臭官口為出納官人中為保夀官
translation: The Five Officers: first mouth second nose third ear fourth eye fifth philtrum; they should be bright and upright not solitary exposed lopsided or slanting. Eye=Supervising-Inspecting ear=Examining-Listening nose=Smelling mouth=Intake-and-Issue philtrum=Longevity-Preserving
notes: FOUR of five titles differ from Taiqing not just the fifth member; ordered enumeration

historicalClaim: one good officer yields ten years of rank; defect or ugliness yields ill fortune
sourcePassageChinese: 或一官好則貴十年或有缺陷者及醜惡者㐫
translation: If one officer is good then ten years of rank; if any is defective or ugly then ill fortune
notes: rank and duration prediction

historicalClaim: the term 'officer' glossed via the Xunzi commentary as to superintend and to discern
sourcePassageChinese: 五官(荀子注司主也又識也)
translation: The Five Officers [gloss: per the commentary on Xunzi 'officer' means to superintend also to discern]
notes: explicit intertextual citation of the Xunzi commentary tradition

historicalClaim: upper=hairline to between brows; middle=between brows to nose tip; lower=tip and philtrum to cheeks/jaw
sourcePassageChinese: 靣之三停自髪際下至眉間為上停自眉間至鼻凖為中停自凖人中至頰為下停
translation: The face's three sections: hairline to between the brows is upper; between the brows to the nose tip is middle; from the tip and philtrum to the cheeks is lower
notes: NEW: REFUTES prior claim that facial thirds has no Siku witness; FACIAL domain distinct from 卷六 body

historicalClaim: the three sections image the Three Powers: upper heaven middle man lower earth
sourcePassageChinese: 夫三停者以像三才也上像天中像人下像地
translation: The three sections image the Three Powers: upper images heaven middle images man lower images earth
notes: cosmological correspondence with no predictive claim attached in this clause

historicalClaim: upper governs rank middle governs longevity lower governs wealth
sourcePassageChinese: 上停長而豐隆方而廣濶者主貴中停隆而凖峻而静者主壽也下停方而滿端而厚者主富也
translation: An upper section long full square and broad governs rank; a middle section full with the tip steep and composed governs longevity; a lower section square full upright and thick governs wealth
notes: rank longevity and wealth predicates all present

historicalClaim: when all three sections are proportionate this is a superior physiognomy
sourcePassageChinese: 三停皆稱乃上相之人矣
translation: When all three sections are proportionate this is a person of superior physiognomy
notes: 稱 family not 平等; facial domain

historicalClaim: upper long great auspiciousness; middle long near the sovereign; lower long common and wandering
sourcePassageChinese: 上停長者大吉昌中停長者近君王下停長者皆庸俗逺走他方主不良
translation: Upper long: great auspiciousness. Middle long: near the sovereign. Lower long: all common and vulgar travelling far portending ill
notes: BODY sections; differential-ranked; MUST NOT be merged with the 卷五 facial rows

historicalClaim: also said: proportionate body thirds indicate wealth and rank
sourcePassageChinese: 又云身三停相稱及上下匀稠則為富貴之人也
translation: It is also said: if the body's three sections are proportionate and upper and lower evenly substantial this is a person of wealth and rank
notes: 又云 marks a secondary layer inside the base text; 相稱 not 平等; explicitly 身三停

historicalClaim: the three sections broadly seek proportion
sourcePassageChinese: 不露不麄不枯槁三停大體求相稱
translation: Not exposed not coarse not withered; the three sections broadly seek proportion
notes: domain unspecified in this verse; third internal witness to the 相稱 predicate

historicalClaim: the three sections equal and able to be harmonious and beautiful
sourcePassageChinese: 三停平等能和美官髙財足志多般
translation: The three sections equal and able to be harmonious and beautiful; office high wealth sufficient aspirations manifold
notes: REFUTES prior claim that 平等 is exclusive to the Shenxiang-quanbian/Mayi lineage; verse context; domain unspecified

condition: form resembles an element and obtains that same element
historicalClaim: five like-with-like pairings each with one outcome
sourcePassageChinese: 似金得金剛毅深似木得木資財阜似水得水文章貴似火得火兵機大似土得上多櫃庫
translation: Resembling metal and obtaining metal: firm resolute deep. Wood: resources and wealth abundant. Water: literary distinction noble. Fire: military strategy great. Earth: many storehouses
notes: exactly FIVE like-with-like pairs NOT a 5x5 grid; text reads 得上 for 得土; wealth rank and character predicates

historicalClaim: each element has a shape it does not object to
sourcePassageChinese: 金不嫌方木不嫌痩水不嫌肥火不嫌尖土不嫌濁
translation: Metal does not object to being square; wood to being lean; water to being stout; fire to being pointed; earth to being turbid
notes: a tolerance rule not a classifier; must not be inverted into colour or shape typing

historicalClaim: wood thin metal square water fat earth thick fire narrow-top broad-base
sourcePassageChinese: NOT_RETRIEVED
translation: wood thin metal square water fat earth thick like a turtle-back top-pointed broad-base is fire
notes: DOWNGRADED; no cleanly licensed machine-readable witness obtained

historicalClaim: the Renlun fengjian agrees with this Five Mountains passage
sourcePassageChinese: (人倫風鑑同)
translation: (The Renlun fengjian agrees.)
notes: collation note inside the base text; names a lost comparandum witness

historicalClaim: the Renlun fengjian agrees with this Four Rivers passage
sourcePassageChinese: (人倫風鑑同)
translation: (The Renlun fengjian agrees.)
notes: second occurrence

historicalClaim: the Renlun fengjian is cited sixteen times in juan one as a variant-reading witness
sourcePassageChinese: (人倫風鑑云隂陽之氣氛氲) … (人倫風鑑洞𤣥經同) … (人倫風鑑千字文同)
translation: (The Renlun fengjian reads: the qi of yin and yang, dense and swirling) … (The Renlun fengjian and the Dongxuan jing agree) … (The Renlun fengjian and the Qianziwen agree)
folio: KR3g0045_WYG_001-1a … 001-6a (16 separate interlinear notes; 2 pinned as passageIds, 14 not individually located)

historicalClaim: each of the nine provinces on the face carries a colour with an outcome
sourcePassageChinese: 雍州白色常潤冀州青黒色主酒色上亡兖州青紅色主吉昌青州青色吉豫州黄色吉
translation: Yong province white colour constantly moist; Ji province blue-black governs death through wine and lust; Yan province blue-red governs auspiciousness; Qing province blue auspicious; Yu province yellow auspicious
section: 九州 (sub-section at 002-10b; the 五嶽…所管屬者 heading governs the preceding similes passage)
notes: E-9: section relabelled 九州. an EXPLICIT colour-to-facial-region relation in the pinned corpus; death predicate present; NOT a licence for modern colour measurement

historicalClaim: the text invokes the ancients' admonition on assessing the mind and choosing one's method
sourcePassageChinese: 此古人有論心擇術之戒也
translation: This is the ancients' admonition on assessing the mind and choosing one's method
notes: NEW: 論心/擇術 is verbatim Xunzi Feixiang vocabulary; a physiognomy manual citing the classic critique of physiognomy

historicalClaim: reading the form is inferior to assessing the mind which is inferior to choosing one's method
sourcePassageChinese: 相形不如論心論心不如擇術
translation: Reading the form is not as good as assessing the mind; assessing the mind is not as good as choosing one's method
notes: DOWNGRADED from VERIFIED_PRIMARY: not retrieved from an inspectable witness in this pass; carry as negative finding; pin against a ctext or Wikisource oldid before promoting

historicalClaim: the face has Twelve Palaces: 命/財帛/兄弟/父母/男女/奴僕/妻妾/疾厄/遷移/官禄/福德 (11 named) + 相貌 as concluding summary; NO 田宅宮
sourcePassageChinese: 或曰面有十二宫印堂為命宫天倉地庫為財帛宫龍虎額角頭為兄弟宫日月角為父母宫三隂三陽為男女宫懸壁為奴僕宫魚尾為妻妾宫神光年夀為疾厄宫山林邊地為遷移宫正面為官禄宫精神地角福堂為福德宫相貌則總而言也
translation: One account holds the face has Twelve Palaces: seal-hall=Life, granaries/treasuries=Wealth, dragon-tiger/forehead-corners=Siblings, sun-moon horns=Parents, three-yin/three-yang=Children, hanging-wall=Servants, fish-tails=Spouse, spirit-light/year-longevity=Adversity, mountain-forest/border-land=Travel, frontal-plane=Office, essence-spirit/earth-corner/blessing-hall=Fortune; countenance is the whole
notes: E-1: refutes the dossier's 十二宮=0. The system IS byte-pinned in the Siku corpus (太清 卷一). Distinct from the received-Mayi/神相全編 mapping (田宅宮, 財帛宮=nose), which stays unpinned/SOURCE_REQUIRED. 11 named palaces + 相貌; fortune-typed.

historicalClaim: 太清 卷三 attributes to 荀子 a maxim ranking heart above form and virtue above heart — but does NOT quote 荀子·非相 verbatim
sourcePassageChinese: 荀子曰相形不如相心論心不如論徳
translation: Xunzi says: reading the form is not as good as reading the heart; assessing the heart is not as good as assessing virtue
notes: E-2: the EXPLICIT 荀子曰 citation, separate object from the tq-j3-lunxin-zeshu allusion (003-1b) — do NOT cross-upgrade. VARIANT: 太清 reads 相心+論徳; 玉管 卷中 reads 相心+論擇術; received 非相 reads 論心+擇術. The manuals adapt Xunzi, they do not quote him.
